title: The finished report shows per-axle results and findings per row
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a technician with 'Work order lines - Create & Edit', on the build under test.
  • A completed inspection with per-axle fields carrying mixed verdicts across positions and rows.
custom_steps:
1. Confirm the completed read-only view shows each field's verdict: on a per-axle field each position's value and verdict and the axle's verdict, with no verdict per measurement row, and that the phone shows the same as the desktop (the report follows S13-R0).
2. Confirm counting is per axle (an axle contributes one count carrying the worst verdict of its positions), and the inspection list, report counters and field summary report the same numbers; the one exception is the per-axle field's header on the fill screen, which counts flagged positions (for example '2 positions Not OK · 1 Monitor') and names no unit.
3. Confirm a count is not a finding: each flagged row produces its own finding for the work order, naming the axle and the row so a line traces to the measurement, and naming every flagged position on the row with its reading.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The completed read-only view shows each field's verdict. A per-axle field shows each position's value and verdict and the axle's verdict; a measurement row has no verdict of its own.
  • The phone shows the same as the desktop, and the report follows S13-R0.
  • Counting is per axle — an axle contributes one count carrying the worst verdict of its positions — and the inspection list, the report counters and the field's own summary report the same numbers.
  • The one exception is the per-axle field's header on the fill screen, which counts flagged positions for the technician (for example '2 positions Not OK · 1 Monitor') and names no unit.
  • Each flagged row produces its own finding for the work order, naming the axle and the row, so a line can be traced to the measurement that caused it.
  • The finding names every flagged position on the row with its reading.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-8181, story SV-9106 (S8 — Record measurements per axle); Digital Inspections V2 specification, Confluence page 768507905, section S8; read on 22 September 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S8-R24: “The completed read-only view will show each field's verdict. A per-axle field shows each position's value and verdict and the axle's verdict; a measurement row has no verdict of its own. The phone shows the same as the desktop. The report follows S13-R0”
  • S8-R25: “Counting will be per axle, as S5-R20 defines it: an axle contributes one count and carries the worst verdict of the positions on it. The inspection list, the report counters and the field's own summary will report the same numbers. A count is not a finding — S8-R26 produces one finding per flagged row. A count answers how many things need attention; a finding says what each one is. The one exception is the per-axle field's header on the fill screen, which counts flagged positions for the technician, for example '2 positions Not OK · 1 Monitor'. It names no unit, because a row knows its scope but not whether it measures a tire or a brake”
  • S8-R26: “Each flagged row will produce its own finding for the work order, naming the axle and the row, so a line can be traced to the measurement that caused it. The finding names every flagged position on the row with its reading”

Amended on 5 October 2026
S8-R26 gained a sentence on 29 September 2026, and S8-R24 and S8-R25 changed on 5 October 2026 (Digital Inspections V2 specification, Confluence page 768507905 (read on 5 October 2026)). The completed view shows no verdict per measurement row and the phone matches the desktop; the per-axle field's header on the fill screen counts flagged positions; the finding names every flagged position with its reading. The quotes above are the current wording, and the steps and expected results follow them. The printed report is checked manually.

Last checked against build v26.36.8-2a64085 on 10/1/2026.

AUTOMATION: READY
